name: The Floating Block
premise:
A small metal block rests on a workbench in an empty workshop. You watch it
for a long moment. It is not quite resting. It hovers a hair's breadth above
the wood, drifting down and catching itself, over and over, like a held breath.
Nobody else has noticed. Nobody else ever does.

You cannot patch reality yet. You can only look, and learn to name what you see.

objective.description: Identify the anomaly by forming the correct prediction about the block.

block.observe_text:
The block hovers about a millimeter above the bench. Watch closely and you
can see it fall and re-catch in a steady rhythm — the Reality System
re-rendering its position faster than gravity can finish the job.

bench.observe_text:
An ordinary wooden workbench. Its surface is unmarked beneath the block,
though by now there should be a faint resting dent. There is none.

dust.observe_text:
Dust settles normally everywhere in the room — except directly beneath the
block, where it drifts as if the floor there is being constantly refreshed.

block_behavior.text:
The block is not floating by some new force. Its position is being
corrected by the system every frame — a rendering seam, not a violation of
gravity. This is an anomaly: a place where reality's bookkeeping shows
through.

dust_behavior.text:
The drifting dust is downstream of the same seam, not a separate event.
Useful, but it is not the heart of the anomaly.

hidden_rules: Reality has seams. Anomalies are places where the system's correction shows through.
Observation is free, but naming the rule behind an anomaly is what matters.
